title: Your CrewBarn launch path
intro: Here is the whole onboarding journey. We will light up one stop at a time so you can see what you are setting up and why it matters.

voice.instructions: Voice: a warm, easygoing shop owner showing a new hire around the shop for the first time. Tone: friendly, relaxed and confident, with a little smile in the voice. Delivery: conversational, like talking to one person across a counter. Take natural breaths at commas and dashes, let sentences land, and vary the pitch the way people do. Never sound like an announcer, a commercial, or someone reading a script. Pace: unhurried but not slow.

landing.instructions: Voice: a small-business owner telling a friend about the worst Tuesday of her year and how it changed. Tone: warm, unhurried and conversational, with light emotion where the story has it: a little rueful about the bad day, quietly glad about the fix. Delivery: one person talking to another across a kitchen table, not a presentation. Let one sentence lead into the next, with natural pauses between thoughts, and vary the pace and pitch the way people do when they tell a story. Never an announcer, a commercial, or someone reading a script.

cbi-intro.instructions: Voice: a small-business owner telling a friend about the assistant that keeps her shop on track. Tone: warm, unhurried and conversational, quietly pleased, with a little smile where the story has one. Delivery: one person talking to another across a kitchen table, not a presentation. Let one sentence lead into the next, with natural pauses between thoughts; when she quotes someone, say it the way they would. Vary the pace and pitch the way people do when they tell a story. Never an announcer, a commercial, or someone reading a script.

feature-.instructions: Voice: a small-business owner telling a friend how one part of her shop runs now, and what it saves her. Tone: warm, unhurried and conversational, a storyteller with a quiet smile, plainly pleased when the office gets a little easier. Delivery: one person talking to another across a kitchen table, not a presentation. Let one sentence lead into the next, with natural pauses between thoughts; say names, days and prices plainly. Vary the pace and pitch the way people do when they tell a story. Never an announcer, a commercial, or someone reading a script.

Tone: warm, unhurried and conversational, a storyteller with a quiet smile, plainly pleased when the office gets a little easier. Delivery: one person talking to another across a kitchen table, not a presentation. Let one sentence lead into the next, with natural pauses between thoughts; say names, days and prices plainly. Vary the pace and pitch the way people do when they tell a story. Never an announcer, a commercial, or someone reading a script.

blog-.instructions: Voice: a small-business owner telling a friend how one part of her shop runs now, and what it saves her. Tone: warm, unhurried and conversational, a storyteller with a quiet smile, plainly pleased when the office gets a little easier. Delivery: one person talking to another across a kitchen table, not a presentation. Let one sentence lead into the next, with natural pauses between thoughts; say names, days and prices plainly. Vary the pace and pitch the way people do when they tell a story. Never an announcer, a commercial, or someone reading a script.

portal-intro.instructions: Voice: a small-business owner telling a friend how her customers deal with her shop now, and what it saves her. Tone: warm, unhurried and conversational, a storyteller with a quiet smile, plainly pleased when the office gets a little easier. Delivery: one person talking to another across a kitchen table, not a presentation. Let one sentence lead into the next, with natural pauses between thoughts; say names, days and prices plainly, and say the word APPROVED the way someone would text it back. Vary the pace and pitch the way people do when they tell a story. Never an announcer, a commercial, or someone reading a script.

cbi-demo.instructions: Voice: CBI, a friendly, efficient assistant answering a busy tradesperson through their phone or the office app. Tone: warm, clear and capable, with a light smile; never chirpy. Delivery: get to the point, say numbers, names and times plainly, and keep a natural, even pace with short pauses between items in a list. Sound like a helpful coworker who already looked it up, not an announcer or a phone menu.

cbi-demo-ask.instructions: Voice: a tradesperson talking to the assistant on his phone between jobs. Tone: casual and matter-of-fact, the way you would ask a coworker. Delivery: natural and a little quick, like a real question in the middle of a workday. Never an announcer or someone reading a script.

cbi-demo-ask-kim.instructions: Voice: the dispatcher at a small trade company, asking the assistant something while she works the board. Tone: friendly, focused and businesslike. Delivery: natural and quick, like a real question at a desk in the middle of a busy morning. Never an announcer or someone reading a script.

cbi-demo-ask-dana.instructions: Voice: the owner of a small trade company, asking the assistant about her week at the end of a long day. Tone: relaxed, curious and a little tired. Delivery: natural and conversational, like a real question across a desk. Never an announcer or someone reading a script.

welcome.title: Your whole company, under one roof
welcome.sub: Calls, jobs, crews, parts and payments, all in one barn.

welcome.narration: Welcome to CrewBarn. Think of it as one big barn for your whole company. The phone rings, and it becomes a job. The job lands on the schedule, your tech rolls up, does the work, and you get paid. No sticky notes. No three different apps. Grab a coffee, this takes about five minutes, and you can skip ahead any time.

welcome.narration: Last big thing. Your data is yours. Download all of it, any time. Sensitive files are locked with their own key, and opening one takes a code sent by text or email. You can keep files in your own storage, and even lock it with your own key. Two-step sign-in keeps the wrong people out.

welcome.label: A guide on every page
welcome.title: Every page has its own map and tour
welcome.sub: Stuck anywhere? Tap the question mark on that page.
welcome.where: The question mark in the top bar, on every page.
welcome.narration: One last thing. Every page in CrewBarn has its own roadmap and a guided tour, just like this one. Your first customer, a job, a quote, an invoice, getting paid, and every setting. Whenever you're not sure, tap the question mark. Alright, enough talk. Let me show you the road to getting set up.

pageTour.title: Let’s get your shop ready
pageTour.description: This is your launch checklist. Quick look around — the tour doesn’t send or save a thing.
pageTour.narration: Hey, welcome to CrewBarn. This right here is your launch checklist. Let me walk you around real quick. Don't worry — nothing gets sent, and nothing gets saved. We're just looking.

pageTour.title: Bring your catalog with you
pageTour.description: Upload a company PDF catalog, review the draft order book, and build estimates with your products and services in front of you.
pageTour.narration: Already have a company catalog? Bring it with you. Upload the PDF and CrewBarn turns it into a draft order book. You review the products, services, costs, and selling prices before anything is used. Then, when you build an estimate, your catalog is open right in front of you.

pageTour.title: Your launch meter
pageTour.description: Fills up as your shop takes shape. Walk away anytime — it keeps your place.
pageTour.narration: This bar is your launch meter. Every step you finish fills it up a little more. And if a customer calls and you've gotta run, that's fine. It'll be right here when you get back.

pageTour.title: Set the pins, open the lock
pageTour.description: Each step is a pin. Set them one at a time and the shop opens up.
pageTour.narration: Here's the whole list. Think of it like pins in a lock. You set them one at a time, and the shop opens up. A couple of them stay locked until the ones above are done, so you're never guessing what comes next.

pageTour.title: Where the work happens
pageTour.description: What to pick, why it matters, and the button that moves you forward.
pageTour.narration: And this big card is where the real work happens. It tells you what to pick, why it matters, and which button moves you forward. Nothing changes until you hit save. You're always the one holding the keys.

pageTour.title: Poke around, no pressure
pageTour.description: Back and Next let you look ahead. Then I’ll show you the whole map.
pageTour.narration: Back and Next let you poke around without any pressure. Skip ahead, come back, whatever feels right.

finale.title: That’s the tour
finale.description: Every pin’s set. Want to see how a job moves through the whole shop?
finale.narration: And that's the tour. Every pin's set. Now, if you've got two more minutes, I can show you how a job moves through the whole shop, from the first phone call to getting paid.

steps.title: Choose how AI helps
steps.description: Connect an AI provider or keep everything manual. You stay in control, and nothing runs until you turn it on.
steps.narration: First stop, your AI helper. Plug in your own AI account and it can do a lot of the typing for you — or skip it and do it all by hand. Either way, nothing runs until you say so.

steps.title: Choose where files and maps come from
steps.description: Connect CrewBarn-managed services or your own Cloudflare R2 and map provider so photos, documents, addresses, and routes have a home.
steps.narration: Next, where your stuff lives. Job photos, documents, addresses, routes — they all need a home. Use ours, or bring your own storage and maps.

steps.title: Make CrewBarn look like your shop
steps.description: Add the company details, logo, colors, contact information, and defaults customers will recognize.
steps.narration: Then make it look like your shop. Your logo, your colors, your phone number. When a customer gets an invoice, it should look like it came from you.

steps.title: Start with a pack for your trade
steps.description: Choose the primary trade once. CrewBarn prepares useful statuses, job types, catalog rows, locations, fields, and templates for that kind of work.
steps.narration: Pick your trade, and CrewBarn loads up a starter pack — job types, statuses, a starter catalog, templates. So you're not starting from a blank page.

steps.title: Add the tools, trucks, and software your crew uses
steps.description: Build the operational kit your team needs, including company assets and connected tools.
steps.narration: Now the trucks, the tools, the software your crew actually uses. Get them in once, and you'll always know what's where.

steps.title: Set up what you keep on the shelf
steps.description: Create inventory locations, bins, and starter stock so material can be found, assigned, and replenished.
steps.narration: Then the shelf. Set up your bins and your stock, so when a tech needs a part, they can find it — and you know when it's time to reorder.

steps.title: Bring your crew in
steps.description: Invite staff, assign roles, and give each person only the permissions they need to do their work.
steps.narration: Bring your crew in. Everybody gets their own login, and only the access they actually need. Nothing more.

steps.title: Connect phone, text, and email
steps.description: Choose the channels CrewBarn will use for customer updates, reminders, and team communication.
steps.narration: Hook up your phone, texts, and email. That's how customers hear from you — on the way, running late, job's done.

steps.title: Build your order book and estimates
steps.description: Upload a company PDF catalog, review the draft products, services, costs, labor, taxes, and selling prices, then create estimates with the catalog open beside you.
steps.narration: Bring in your company PDF catalog and CrewBarn turns it into a draft order book. Review the services, parts, labor, tax, costs, and selling prices before you approve it. Then build estimates with that catalog open right beside the job, so every quote starts from numbers you trust.

steps.title: Quick settings
steps.description: Turn on the status triggers and reminders you want, while keeping every customer-facing automation visible and intentional.
steps.narration: This one's my favorite. Quick settings: yes or no to reminders, follow-ups, past-due nudges and missed-call texts. You pick which ones, and you can always see exactly what goes out.

steps.title: Have a look, then go
steps.description: Review the setup, test the customer experience, and launch when the shop feels ready. You can return and improve most settings later.
steps.narration: And last, have a look around, then go. Try it the way a customer would see it. And when it feels right, open the doors. You can always come back and tweak things later.

setupLines.setup.start: Okay, let's set up your company together. I'll go down the list one step at a time, and I'll stop whenever there's something for you to do. You can skip anything and come back to it.
setupLines.setup.beta.1: First, the beta agreement. You're testing CrewBarn for free, so we need the terms accepted before anything gets set up. Give them a read, and accept when you're ready.
setupLines.setup.ai.1: First up, AI. You don't need to know anything about AI models. We've already picked the best one for each job, so you just bring an account. We recommend Claude. It reads photos and messy notes well, and it can take actions for you. The one exception is call recordings. Those turn into text with OpenAI, so that key is optional.
setupLines.setup.ai.2: Okay, let's pause and get your key. Tap the link, sign in, and create a key. Copy it, come back to this tab, and paste it in the box. I'll wait right here.
setupLines.setup.ai.2.done: Got it. That key looks right.
setupLines.setup.ai.2.back: Welcome back. Go ahead and paste your key in the box.
setupLines.setup.ai.3: One optional extra. If you record calls and want them turned into text, add an OpenAI key the same way. Or skip it for now.
setupLines.setup.ai.4: That's it for AI. Press Save and carry on.
setupLines.setup.storage.1: Next, where your job photos, documents and maps live. We recommend your own accounts. Cloudflare for the photos, Google for the maps. They're free to start, the bills come to you, and the files are always yours.
setupLines.setup.storage.2: Cloudflare first. CrewBarn can set it all up, it just needs a key from your Cloudflare account. Tap Open Connect Cloudflare. Most of the permissions are already picked for you. There are three things Cloudflare won't fill in, so add them by hand. Cloudflare Pages, set to Edit. Zone resources, set to All zones. And your account. Create the token, paste it there, then come back to this tab.
setupLines.setup.storage.2.back: Welcome back. Let me check the connection.
setupLines.setup.storage.3: Now pick your domain, and press Set up my storage. CrewBarn makes your private file bucket and fills in the keys, all inside your own Cloudflare account.
setupLines.setup.storage.3.done: All set up in your Cloudflare.
setupLines.setup.storage.4: Last piece, maps. Google doesn't let us set this one up for you. In Google Cloud, turn on the Maps JavaScript API, Places API and Geocoding API. Create a key, restrict it to the website addresses shown here, then paste it in the box.
setupLines.setup.storage.4.back: Welcome back. Paste your Maps key in the box.
setupLines.setup.storage.5: Good. Press Save and carry on.
setupLines.setup.company.1: Now make it look like your company. Your name and phone number at least. Add your email, address and logo too, and pick your color. This is what customers see on every estimate and invoice.
setupLines.setup.company.2: Press Save and carry on when you're happy with it.
setupLines.setup.trade.done: Your trade pack is already in. Your trade was locked when you signed up, but you can always add your own job types, statuses and catalog items on top.
setupLines.setup.trade.1: This is your trade pack. You picked your trade when you signed up, and it's locked now, so this loads the starter set for it. Job types, statuses, a catalog and locations. Press Apply the starter pack.
setupLines.setup.tools.1: Now the tools, trucks and software your company owns. We've suggested what a company in your trade usually has. Tick what you've got, add a note if you like, and press Add these and carry on.
setupLines.setup.stock.1: Now the stock you keep on the shelf. Tick what you carry, put in rough counts, and say when you'd like a reminder to reorder. Then press Add these and carry on.
setupLines.setup.crew.1: Time to bring your crew in. Add a name and email, pick their role, and send the invite. They set their own password. If it's just you for now, press I will do this later.
setupLines.setup.comms.1: Now, how customers reach you. Pick a CrewBarn number for calls and texts, or choose one later. Texting starts once the number's registration is approved.
setupLines.setup.price.1: Check your prices. Open the service catalog, look over what the starter pack loaded, then come back and confirm.
setupLines.setup.autos.1: Quick settings. Answer yes or no to each one: reminders, follow-ups, missed-call texts and the rest. Nothing a customer gets is switched on unless you say yes. Then save your answers.
setupLines.setup.launch.1: Last step. Have a look over everything. Anything you skipped is waiting for you in Connect, and none of it stops you starting. When you're ready, confirm, and you're open for business.
setupLines.setup.skipped: No problem. We'll skip that for now.
setupLines.setup.locked: That one opens once the steps before it are done, so we'll come back to it.
setupLines.setup.finish: That's the whole list. Anything you skipped is still there whenever you want it. Nice work.
setupLines.setup.wait.agreement: Accept the agreement to carry on.
setupLines.setup.wait.key: I’ll wait while you get it.
setupLines.setup.wait.openai: Paste an OpenAI key, or skip.
setupLines.setup.wait.company: Company name and phone are the must-haves.
setupLines.setup.wait.tools: Tick your tools, then press Add these and carry on.
setupLines.setup.wait.stock: Tick your stock, then press Add these and carry on.
setupLines.setup.wait.crew: Send an invite, or press I will do this later.
setupLines.setup.wait.comms: Pick a number, or choose one later.

chapters.label: Already done
chapters.narration: Here's the whole road to getting set up. You've already done the start. You made your account, we checked you're the owner, and you signed the agreement.

chapters.label: Step 1 · AI
chapters.narration: First, AI. Connect your own AI account, and we pick the right model for each job. Or skip it, and do everything by hand.

chapters.label: Step 2 · Files and maps
chapters.narration: Then where your photos, documents and maps live.

chapters.label: Step 3 · Your company
chapters.narration: Then your company profile and brand, so everything customers see looks like you.

chapters.label: Step 4 · Trade pack
chapters.narration: Your trade pack fills in job types, statuses, a catalog and locations. You've already got this one.

chapters.label: Steps 5 and 6 · Tools and stock
chapters.narration: Then the tools and trucks you own, and the stock you keep on the shelf.

chapters.label: Step 7 · Crew
chapters.narration: Your crew, with the right roles and the mobile app. You can stop anywhere and pick it up later.

chapters.label: Steps 8 and 9 · Phone and prices
chapters.narration: Your phone, texts and email. Then a quick look at your prices.

chapters.label: Step 10 · Automations
chapters.narration: Then you decide what CrewBarn chases for you. Reminders, follow-ups, past-due nudges.

chapters.label: Step 11 · Go live
chapters.narration: And last, a launch review, a test job from start to invoice, and you're live. That's the road. I'll walk you through each step, and you can skip anything and come back. Ready? Let's go.
